newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bolsters navy patrols near Malaysia border.
newsitem.headline: Manila bolsters navy patrols near Malaysia border.

text.p: The Philippines military said on Monday it had sent more navy ships to patrol its border with Malaysia after police accused a group of Malaysians of abducting seven Filipinos from a village in the country's southwest.

Regional commander Major-General Reynaldo Reyes said he had ordered the strengthened patrols after talking to residents of Mangsee village near Palawan island where the alleged incident occurred on April 15.

On Sunday a Manila presidential palace statement, quoting police sources, said what looked like a Malaysian navy patrol craft landed on Mangsee. It said a group of Malaysians took away seven villagers they had accused of stealing their boat engines.

Malaysia and the Philippines are separated only by a narrow strip of water and there have been frequent reports from both sides of intrusions into each other's territory. Piracy is also rampant in the area.

In Kuala Lumpur, Malaysian Defence Minister Syed Hamid Albar said on Monday his ministry was investigating the alleged incident but initial inquiries showed no Malaysian navy personnel were involved, the official Bernama news agency said.
Philippine President Fidel Ramos has also ordered an investigation.
Senators said if the incident was confirmed, Manila should file a protest with Kuala Lumpur.
Senator Juan Ponce Enrile said the only way to prevent similar incidents was for the government to strengthen its navy, whose fleet consists mostly of vessels of World War Two vintage.
"The only antidote to this (incident) is for the country to wake up and provide the military with the means to maintain its dignity, honour and security," Enrile told reporters.
Defence Secretary Renato de Villa said relations between the two countries were excellent and diplomacy should be used in resolving the problem.
